newsitem.title: CANADA: CWB says no comment on Brazil but price looks low.
newsitem.headline: CWB says no comment on Brazil but price looks low.

text.p: A Canadian Wheat Board spokesman declined comment on rumors the CWB sold up to 600,000 tonnes of wheat to Brazil overnight but also said the rumored price of US$150 a tonne, FOB St. Lawrence, looked too low.

"We have ongoing business there (Brazil). I can't confirm or not that we've sold a quantity in there but I will tell you that those prices are overly bearish," CWB spokesman Brian Stacey told Reuters in an interview.
Asked if US$150/tonne was too low, Stacey said: "Yes."
Trade sources said earlier Tuesday, the CWB sold up to 600,000 tonnes to Brazilian millers at US$150/tonne.

"If you're looking at late June, July for No3 Canada Western Soft White Spring wheat would be around US$155 (a tonne) and of course there would be premiums to that if they wanted No1s and No2s," Stacey said.
"And in the case of old crop for May position, probably US$15 to US$20 a tonne over the US$155. That would be US$170 to US$175," Stacey added.
